landingV2.welcome_subtitle: Coding lover and problem solver, building solutions that make hard tasks easier and automating the easy ones.
landingV2.detail.portfolio.sections.over: My personal portfolio, built as an Angular micro-frontend system inside an Nx monorepo. A shell app owns the router and mounts the landing, odontogram and damoclesSword remotes at runtime, so each app ships on its own.

Nx was the starting point. I wanted several independent apps that could be built, tested and deployed separately, plus a place to practise building small, reusable libraries. As the project grew, that structure kept everything easy to understand and reuse. The shell is the only host; every other app is a remote it composes at runtime through Module Federation.
landingV2.detail.portfolio.sections.micr: The honest reason is learning. I wanted to understand micro-frontends properly, and building one taught me far more than reading about them ever could.

Beyond that, the runtime composition earns its keep. Moving between apps never reloads Angular or the shared libraries, shared configuration lives in one place, and locale-first routing works across every app in a way separate per-app deployments could not offer. For a portfolio it is deliberately over-engineered, and that is the point: the site is itself a showcase of how the pieces fit together.
landingV2.detail.portfolio.sections.loca: The first URL segment is the language, like /en/projects/portfolio. That makes every page shareable and cacheable per locale, and a pair of route guards keep the URL and the active language in sync.

A locale guard resolves the desired language on entry and a correction guard rewrites the URL when it drifts, so a stale segment never fights the active locale. Translations run through RokuTranslator, a small i18next wrapper I built by hand instead of reaching for a general library. It is a framework agnostic singleton shared across the whole federation, each library registers its own namespace with per-locale lazy loaders, and switching language at runtime needs no rebuild. Forcing it to a strict singleton in the Module Federation config is what stops the locale from fragmenting between apps.
landingV2.detail.portfolio.sections.libr: Code is grouped by scope under libs, and something earns its own library only when it is a real feature or genuinely reusable. Everything crosses a boundary through its path alias, never a relative path.

A component usually starts inside the app that needs it and moves to the shared library only once a second app actually reuses it. The rule for shared code is that it must be usable without much configuration; when it is not, I keep two focused components and extract the common piece rather than ship one component buried in options. RokuTranslator is the clearest case for its own library: framework agnostic, used everywhere, and revised often enough that I did not want it destabilising the shared UI. Icons follow the same spirit, small standalone components rather than inline SVG.
landingV2.detail.portfolio.sections.engi: Signals drive change detection everywhere, work loads lazily by default, and the whole workspace ships through a custom Docker toolchain onto a small Kubernetes cluster.

State runs on signals with event coalescing on, so Angular does the least change-detection work it can. A custom Nx plugin, @portfolio/docker, wraps docker buildx with build and push executors, and Helm deploys the workspace to a k3s cluster. GitHub Actions computes the affected projects on every push and runs the pipeline through staging before a tagged production release. Tests are Jest for units and Cypress or Playwright for end to end, all pointed at the shell, because the shell is how the apps are actually used.
landingV2.detail.odontogram.what_body: A full odontogram for recording dental treatments and keeping each patient's history over time.
landingV2.detail.odontogram.hard_part_bo: A tooth has up to six zones, and a single treatment can affect several zones and span more than one tooth. The SVG chart maps every click back to the right zone and tooth, and persists the resulting state.
landingV2.detail.damocles.studio_body: A VR game studio founded by a group of university students who decided to build their own games using a technology that is still not standardized: virtual reality. Alongside their own titles, the studio also offers VR and gamification services to other companies.
landingV2.detail.damocles.work_body: STARLIT: ASCENSION, a VR shooter currently under development, sits alongside client R&D work such as Realistic Interactor and the VR Sickness Reducer, a graduated-exposure test built to reduce VR-induced dizziness.
landingV2.detail.damocles.built_body: An Angular micro-frontend with Home, About, Services and Contact pages sharing a component system translated into English, Spanish and French, a reactive contact form, and a data-access layer for news and projects.
